subject: Staged reserved commit proposal & GPU-index fallback - NimbleAI
messages:
From: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@nimble.ai>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Cc: Ella Park <ella.park@nimble.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity - pricing guardrails and fallback options

Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We like Redwood's deterministic latency and the model routing ideas — exactly what we need for our inference-heavy features. Before we move to an LOI, procurement asked for a concrete committed capacity proposal. Two constraints from our side:

- We want a 12-month reserve with the ability to phase up in tranches (0-6-12 months).
- Procurement is concerned about GPU-market volatility; they asked for a clear fallback if spot/market prices spike >25% (either credits or a short-term downgrade path).

Can you share a priced term sheet and suggest how you typically structure a "fallback" or escrow mechanism? We shared our initial usage profile in the attached.

Thanks,
Carl Jensen
Head of Platform, NimbleAI
Attachments: NimbleAI_capacity_sheet_v3.xlsx
From: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
To: Carl Jensen <carl.jensen@nimble.ai>
Cc: Ella Park <ella.park@nimble.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity - pricing guardrails and fallback options

Carl — really appreciate the clear ask and the usage sheet. High level response below; attaching a short draft term sheet with phasing options.

Key proposal (short):
- 12-month committed pool, billed monthly.
- Phased activation: 40% baseline in month 1, +30% month 6, +30% month 12. You only pay for active tranche capacity.
- GPU-index fallback: if GPU market price (NVIDIA spot index) increases >25% for a 30-day rolling window, we trigger one of two client-choice remedies: (A) one-month credit equal to the incremental cost above the 25% threshold applied to the affected tranche; or (B) temporary downgrade to compatible lower-cost model variant for up to 60 days for affected requests (same SLOs for latency).

We typically route this through a discount escrow (small portion of commit held in an interest-bearing escrow to fund credits) + an operational downgrade playbook. Pricing in the draft assumes a 15% reserve discount for the 12-month commit with tranche billing.

Next steps: 1) Can you confirm Nimble prefers Credit (A) or Downgrade (B) as primary? 2) I'll loop in Marissa (finance) and Karthik (pricing) to firm up the economics and sign-off path.

Best,
Rohan Mehta
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_term_sheet_draft.pdf
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Reserved capacity - pricing guardrails and fallback options

Rohan / Karthik — forwarding Carl's note and my quick read on the draft term sheet. TL;DR: we can cover a conservative fallback but need to lock the trigger definition and cap exposure. Points for pricing approval meeting:

1) Trigger definition: we need a single public index (prefer NVDA spot composite) and require 30-day rolling exceedance >25% to avoid churn.
2) Cap exposure: recommend escrow capped at 8% of committed ARR for the first 12 months; beyond that, finance reviews renewal exposure.
3) Downgrade option: operationally feasible, but we need an SLA guarantee for latency and a rollback plan; ops should own runbook.
4) Discount: 15% for 12-month base looks doable with tranche billing; if Nimble selects Credit (A) we should tighten the credit calculus (cap credits to 50% of escrow in any 30-day window).

I propose a 30-min sync today to approve numbers for a quick LOI. Karthik — can you run a worst-case P&L (GPU price +50% scenario) using the attached Nimble usage profile and return a hit estimate before 3pm?

—Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Carl — quick update after internal review. Thanks for picking option B (Ella confirmed preference in our call). Below is the refined runnable proposal we can include in the LOI: 

1) Phased activation (unchanged): 40% / +30% (month 6) / +30% (month 12).
2) Discount & billing: 15% committed discount applied to base tranche; monthly invoices with tranche activation reconciliation.
3) GPU-index fallback (primary: Downgrade option):
   - Trigger: NVIDIA spot composite index >25% above baseline (baseline = average prior 90 days) sustained for 30-day rolling window.
   - Remedy: Redwood may surface a compatible quantized model variant or lower-memory engine for impacted requests for up to 60 days. During this period Redwood will: (a) maintain 99th pctl latency SLO; (b) provide token-level quality regressions report; (c) provide customer opt-out window for specific routes.
   - Escrow: we will still create a small escrow equal to 3% of first-year committed ARR to cover transition ops and engineering hours; credits only used if operational rollback occurs and documented SLA breaches are found.
4) Caps: Total financial exposure from credits (if ever used) capped at 8% of committed ARR in year 1.

Attached is a redline-ready term sheet and a DocuSign LOI link if Nimble is comfortable (link below). If that looks good I'll ask Legal to prepare the formal LOI and Marissa to prepare the escrow mechanics. Can we target LOI signature by next Wednesday (2026-12-02)?
